 This Mfa Is Filed U/S 23 Of Railway Claims
Tribunal Act, Against The Order Dt.Oa Ii U 12/2012 On
The File Of The Railway Claims Tribunal, Bangalore
Bench, Bangalore, Not Allowing The Clim Application
For Compensation.

This Appeal Coming On For Hearing This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section 23(1) of the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987 (for short, 'the Act')
by applicants challenging the order dated 18.09.2014 passed by Railway Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru (for short, 'the Tribunal') in O.A.II U 12/2012.
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
3. The brief facts of the case are that on 20.05.2011 deceased Fakruddin Sab @ Fakru along with his friend Ameer Sab had boarded the train bearing No.56913 from Arasikere.
When deceased was traveling in the said train, he fell down, suffered an injury and succumbed to the injuries.
On the information given by his friend Ameer Sab, the applicants have come to know that Fakruddin Sab had dead.
The applicants being the wife and children of the deceased filed an application before the Claims Tribunal under Section 16 of the Railway Claims Tribunal Act, 1987 seeking compensation.
To prove the case, first applicant has been examined as AW1, one Ameer Sab has been examined as AW2 and Dr.Umadevi has been examined as AW3 and produced 11 documents.
The respondent has examined one Sanjay Kumar as RW1 and produced one document.
On appreciation of the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal has dismissed the application.
Being aggrieved by the same, the applicants have field this appeal before this Court.

4. Sri. Sridhar N Hegde, learned counsel appearing for the applicants has contended that the three witnesses have categorically stated that the deceased while traveling in the train has fallen down,
suffered injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
Even the medical records show that deceased died while he was traveling in the train.
Therefore, he contended that by adducing evidence and producing documents, the claimants have discharged their initial burden.
Now the burden is shifted on the railways to disprove the case of the claimants.
They have examined Sri Sanjay Kumar.
He has also submitted that one Sri Parameshwar Nayak was informed that one passenger while crossing was run over by the train bearing No.56913.
Sri Parameshwar Nayak has not been examined.
Railways have not discharged their burden.

Under the circumstances, the Tribunal has erred in Smt Hussain Bi vs The Union Of India on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14285624/
2 dismissing the claim petition.

sentences.text: 5. Per contra, Sri Abhinay T, learned counsel appearing for the Railways has contended that deceased was not a bonafide passenger.
No ticket has been recovered from the body of the deceased.
The claimants have not proved that the deceased was traveling in the train No.56913 and he fell down, sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
On the other hand, they have contended that when the deceased was crossing the track, train bearing No.56913 ran over and he died.
Since he was an illegal trespasser, he is not entitled for any compensation as per Section 124-A(b) of the Railways Act and the Tribunal has rightly rejected the application.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award.
7.
The case of the applicants is that on 20.05.2011 deceased Fakruddin Sab @ Fakru along with his friend one Ameen Sab boarded the train bearing No.56913 in Arasikere after purchasing the ticket.
When they were traveling in the train, the deceased was standing near the door, due to the high speed and jerk, he fell down from the running train, suffered an injury and succumbed to the same.
To prove the case, they have examined the first applicant as PW1, Ameer Sab has been examined as PW2 and Dr. Umadevi has been examined as PW3 and they have produced 11 documents.
The witness examined in favour of the applicant has categorically stated that deceased was traveling in the train bearing No.56913.
When he was traveling in the train, he lost balance due to the high speed and jerk, fell down from the train, suffered injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
To disprove the case of the applicants, except examining Sanjay Kumar, the railways have not examined any other witnesses and they have failed to discharge their burden.

In this regard, the Apex Court in the case of UNION OF INDIA vs RINA DEVI reported in (2019)3 SCC 572 has held that mere absence of ticket with the injured/deceased will not negate the claim that he was a bonafide passenger.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Initially the burden will be on the applicant who has to discharge by filing an affidavit stating relevant facts and the burden will have to be shifted on the railways.
The relevant portion is extracted hereunder:

"25. We are unable to uphold the above view as the concept of "self-inflicted injury"
would require intention to inflict such injury and not mere negligence of any particular degree.
Doing so would amount to invoking the principle of contributory negligence which cannot be done in the case of liability based on "no fault theory".

We may in this connection refer to the judgment of this Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sunil Kumar

United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sunil Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: [ United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Sunil Kumar, (2019) 12 SCC 398 : 2017 SCC OnLine SC 1443 : (2017) 13 Scale 652] laying down that plea of negligence of the victim cannot be allowed in claim based on "no fault theory" under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Sunil Kumar, (2019) 12 SCC 398 : 2017 SCC OnLine SC 1443 : (2017) 13 Scale 652]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, we hold that death or injury in the course of boarding or de-boarding a train will be an "untoward incident" entitling a victim to the compensation and will not fall under the proviso to Section 124-A merely on the plea of negligence of the victim as a contributing factor.
26. Conflict of decisions has been pointed out on the subject.
As noticed from the statutory provision, compensation is payable for death or injury of a "passenger".

In Raj Kumari [Raj Kumari v. Union of India, 1992 SCC OnLine MP 96 : 1993 ACJ 846] referring to the scheme of the Railways Smt Hussain Bi vs The Union Of India on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14285624/
3 Act, 1890, it was observed that since travelling without ticket was punishable, the burden was on the Railway Administration to prove that passenger was not a bona fide passenger.

entities.text: Raj Kumari [Raj Kumari v. Union of India, 1992 SCC OnLine MP 96 : 1993 ACJ 846]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Railways Smt Hussain Bi vs The Union Of India on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Railway Administration has special knowledge whether ticket was issued or not.
The 1989 Act also has similar provisions being Sections 55 and 137.
This view has led to an inference that any person dead or injured found on the railway premises has to be presumed to be a bona fide passenger so as to maintain a claim for compensation.

However, the Delhi High Court in Gurcharan Singh [Gurcharan Singh v. Union of India, 2014 SCC OnLine Del 101 : 2015 ACJ 171] held that initial onus to prove death or injury to a bona fide passenger is always on the claimant.

entities.text: Gurcharan Singh [Gurcharan Singh v. Union of India, 2014 SCC OnLine Del 101 : 2015 ACJ 171]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, such onus can shift on the Railways if an affidavit of relevant facts is filed by the claimant.
A negative onus cannot be placed on the Railways.

Onus to prove that the deceased or injured was a bona fide passenger can be discharged even in absence of a ticket if relevant facts are shown that ticket was purchased but it was lost."
8.
Under the circumstances, the findings given by the Tribunal that the respondent proved that deceased died while crossing the track is without any proper evidence.
They have not examined the person who has informed that one person while crossing the track hit by the train.
Therefore, the matter requires to be remitted back to the Tribunal to give one more opportunity to the respondent to discharge its burden.
9. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
The order dated 18.09.2014 in O.A.No.12/2012 passed by the Railway Claims Tribunal, Bangalore Bench is set aside.
The matter is remitted back to the Tribunal for fresh consideration, in accordance with law, within six months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
It is made clear that the Tribunal shall decide the matter without being influenced by any of the observations made in this order.
